subject: Helm chart pinning + Ansible credential vaulting for private deploy

Subject: [PrivDeploy] Helm chart pinning + Ansible creds — initial check
Attachments: helm-values-privdeploy.yaml (yaml), ansible-roles-priv.tar.gz (tar.gz), vault-access-matrix.csv (csv)

Hannah / Irene,

Sharing the initial artifacts for the Acme private deployment runbook. Primary asks for this thread:

1) Confirm a safe approach for pinning Helm charts in our private registry so rollbacks are reliable and we don't rely on mutable tags.
2) Validate that the Ansible roles attached do not embed plaintext credentials and map to the Vault paths we plan to grant to Acme.
3) Quick callout: Acme requires that any credential injected into nodes is auditable and limited to a scoped path — see attached vault-access-matrix.csv.

What I attached:
- helm-values-privdeploy.yaml: initial values for the private stack (comments inline about image tags).
- ansible-roles-priv.tar.gz: trimmed roles for cert provisioning + kubeconfig distribution.
- vault-access-matrix.csv: proposed roles -> vault paths mapping for Acme (redacted in the csv).

Notes / concerns:
- The Helm charts we plan to use are mirrored in our private OCI registry. Currently the CI publishes with tag = build_sha, but there is backward compatibility risk if helm templates reference :latest-type tags somewhere. Want your eyes on whether we should lock on digest (sha256:...) or add Chart.lock to the publish flow.
- Ansible playbooks currently use a small helper that pulls secrets from a local file when running in our CI. That helper will need to be replaced with a direct vault lookup for on-prem runs.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Hannah: can you run the helm-values through the chart linting rules and confirm any mutable tag occurrences?
- Irene: can you review the Ansible roles for secret handling and propose a minimal Vault lookup pattern?

Happy to sync over a 30m if it's easier.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the artifacts and clear asks. Quick read and a short checklist below.

On Mon, 29 Mar 2027 at 09:12, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:

> 2) Validate that the Ansible roles attached do not embed plaintext credentials and map to the Vault paths we plan to grant to Acme.
> 3) Quick callout: Acme requires that any credential injected into nodes is auditable and limited to a scoped path — see attached vault-access-matrix.csv.

High level: agree we should enforce digest pinning for runtime deploys and keep human-friendly tags for CI tracing only. Specific items I can take on: 

- Helm chart pinning:
  - Scan helm-values-privdeploy.yaml for image: tags that don't include digest. I'll run a script to detect mutable tags and prepare a chart.lock recommendation.
  - Recommend we add a CI step that writes a Chart.lock with exact OCI digests and publishes alongside the chart (so the chart archive references exact imageRef).
  - For compatibility, implement a runtime option in our deployer: prefer digest if present, else fail fast. No silent fallback to tags.

- Ansible / secret handling:
  - I flagged the helper you mentioned. If CI uses local files today, we should replace that path with a Vault lookup plugin (HashiVault for now) and gate local-file mode behind an explicit flag for dev only.
  - Need to confirm the auth method for Acme: AppRole vs Kubernetes auth. If nodes will pull secrets directly, k8s auth with bound SA is preferred. If Ansible controller will pull and push, AppRole with narrow policies is better.

Questions for Irene (cc):
- Do we have a short example (playbook + lookup) you can share that we can standardize across repos?
- Any objections to Chart.lock in CI given our current helm-release automation?

If this looks right I'll run the Helm scan today and push results to the INFRA ticket.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: [PrivDeploy] Helm chart pinning + Ansible creds — initial check

Hey team — dug into the roles and sketched a minimal, auditable approach. Notes below; pasted examples are intentionally compact.

On Mon, 29 Mar 2027 at 10:03, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> High level: agree we should enforce digest pinning for runtime deploys and keep human-friendly tags for CI tracing only. Specific items I can take on: 

Helm pinning approach (summary):
- CI publishes chart.tar.gz and records image digest(s) for every image referenced during chart packaging. We should store digest-mapping in Chart.lock and also in our internal artifact metadata (registry manifest).
- Deployer must prefer the digest. Implementation options:
  - Use OCI image references in values.yaml like "registry.example.com/repo/image@sha256:..." generated by CI, or
  - Keep values with a placeholder (like IMAGE_DIGEST_IMAGE1) and have a deploy-time substitution step that replaces placeholders with digests from the chart-lock artifact.
- For rollback safety, bake the digest into the final release record in our deploy DB (release -> imageDigests).

Ansible vault integration options (recommended):
- Replace local-file secret helper with ansible lookup via hvac/hashivault lookup plugin. Example snippet (ansible playbook):
  - name: Pull db password from Vault
    set_fact:
      db_password: "{{ lookup('community.hashi_vault.hashi_vault', 'secret=secret/data/acme/db#password', 'mount_point=secret', 'token={{ vault_token }}') }}"

- Auth pattern choices:
  - If Ansible controller runs inside our infra and authenticates on behalf of nodes, use AppRole with tightly-scoped policies and short-lived secret IDs.
  - If we want node-local fetching, use Kubernetes auth bound to the node service account and let the node request tokens directly.

Security & audit considerations:
- Vault access paths must be unique per customer and minimize broad wildcards (no "secret/*" policies). Your vault-access-matrix.csv looks reasonable but we should tighten a couple of entries (I'll mark them on the doc).
- Avoid embedding any token or credential in Ansible vars. If a bootstrap requires a one-time token, rotate it immediately after use and log the rotation in our audit table.

Small implementation note re: sealed-secrets: If we need k8s-scope secrecy that survives Git pushes, consider sealed-secrets but keep the private sealing key off the repo and rotate it on a schedule. That said, for Acme we should prefer Vault-backed secrets for node-level creds and only use sealed-secrets for cluster-scoped config where necessary.

I attached a quick grep summary as a gist in the INFRA ticket and will add inline comments on your vault-access-matrix.csv.

One more: ops-partner (cc) — any constraints from your side on digest vs tag policy for their mirror? If they can guarantee immutable digests on mirror push, that simplifies things.

- Irene
Irene Choi

Thanks — all great points and actionable. Quick recap and owners: 

1) Helm chart pinning (owner: Hannah)
   - Hannah to run the mutable-tag scan and create a Chart.lock suggestion (due EOD Thu).
   - CI: add step to capture image digests and publish alongside chart (INFRA-4521).

2) Ansible secret handling (owner: Irene)
   - Irene to draft a standard lookup pattern (kitchen-sink playbook + minimal AppRole example) and add to the repo templates (due next Tue).
   - Replace local-file helper with hashivault lookup behind a --dev flag; dev flag must be explicit and documented.

3) Vault policies & audit (owner: Marissa -> coordinate with Acme)
   - I'll tighten the CSV and circulate to Acme for sign-off. We will require per-customer mount points and no wildcard policies.

4) Mirror / registry constraints (owner: ops-partner)
   - ops-partner to confirm mirror can publish and guarantee immutable digests on push. If not, we'll default to storing digests in artifact metadata and abort deploys when digest is missing.

I'll update INFRA-4521 with the actions and link the helm-values change once Hannah pushes her scan. If anyone prefers a quick 20m sync to close blockers, ping me and I'll schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa
